To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic intermittent ethanol (CI) exposure during adolescence impairs spatial and working memory in the radial arm maze, and impairs the ability to acquire progressive-ratio responding, but does not alter the ability to acquire fixed-ratio responding.

adolescent rats are more vulnerable than adult rats to long-term effects of CIE on performance in the RAM task and to the acute effects on ethanol on working memory in the RAM task, but not on operant food-rewarded performance.

adolescent CIE exposure produces enduring effects on the ability of animals to integrate reward and risk information in the RAM and that adolescent, but not adult, CIE exposure increases susceptibility to the acute effects ethanol on spatial memory in the RAM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic alcohol consumption during adolescence and adulthood on spatial learning and memory, food motivation and sensitivity to ethanol in rats.
the neurobehavioral consequences of adolescent alcohol abuse.
the effects of chronic intermittent exposure to ethanol during adolescence on neurobehavioral performance in adulthood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CIE exposure during early adolescence is associated with enduring behavioral and pharmacokinetic changes that are not evident in adulthood.
adolescent CIE exposure is associated with enduring deficits in spatial learning and risk-reward integration and increased sensitivity to the acute effects on ethanol in a working memory task.

CIE exposure during adolescent, but not adult life, results in long-lasting deficits in spatial working memory and increased susceptibility to the acute effects (e.g., working memory deficits) of ethanol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adolescent period is a time of increased vulnerability to the long term effects of ethanol exposure on behavior and acute ethanol sensitivity, but that the effects are not due to a general impairment in learning or memory.

CIE exposure during adolescent, but not adulthood, results in long-term deficits in spatial learning, risk-taking behavior and acute ethanol sensitivity, which are likely to be mediated by enduring pharmacokinetic changes in ethanol metabolism.

adolescent CIE exposure results in a selective vulnerability to the effects of acute ethanol on working memory and that the effects on risk-reward integration and working memory are mediated, in part, by the development of pharmacokinetic tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

adolescent rats exposed to CIE show a persistent deficit in their ability to use the spatial cues in the RAM task to guide their behavior, and this deficit is associated with a decreased sensitivity to the performance disrupting effects of an acute ethanol challenge.
CIE exposure in adolescence, but not in adulthood, can have long-lasting effects on neurobehavioral performance and acute ethanol sensitivity.
CIE during adolescence, but apparently not adulthood, produces enduring effects on risk-taking behavior and acute ethanol sensitivity that are not due to altered ethanol pharmacokinetics.
